services.intro: A GTA has three possible options on the same freight transaction — the option actually exercised decides who pays and whether ITC flows.

scenarios.option: Option 1 — GTA opts forward charge, concessional rate
scenarios.supplier: GTA (registered, has exercised the annual option)
scenarios.itc: GTA cannot claim ITC on inputs used for this supply
scenarios.notes: GTA collects and pays tax itself; recipient pays GTA the invoice amount including GST.

scenarios.option: Option 2 — GTA opts forward charge, regular rate
scenarios.supplier: GTA (registered, has exercised the annual option)
scenarios.itc: GTA can claim full ITC on inputs
scenarios.notes: Chosen when the GTA wants to pass on ITC benefit / claim its own ITC.

scenarios.option: Option 3 — GTA has not opted for forward charge (default)
scenarios.recipient: Factory, society, registered person, body corporate, partnership firm, casual taxable person, or any person registered under GST
scenarios.itc: ITC available to the recipient who pays the RCM tax
scenarios.notes: This is the default position unless the GTA has filed the forward-charge option (Annexure V) for the financial year.

services.exempt_note: GTA services to unregistered individuals (for personal use) and specified exempt categories (e.g. agricultural produce, milk, salt, relief materials, single consignment freight below ₹1,500) are outside GST altogether.

services.intro: Two rate structures exist for the same service, and RCM applies only in one of them.

scenarios.option: Option 1 — Supplier charges concessional rate, no ITC
scenarios.supplier: Any person other than a body corporate, paying GST at 5% (no ITC)
scenarios.itc: ITC available to recipient body corporate on the RCM tax paid
scenarios.notes: Most common case — small operators/individual owners renting vehicles to companies.

scenarios.option: Option 2 — Supplier charges regular rate, with ITC
scenarios.supplier: Any person charging GST at 12% (claiming full ITC)
scenarios.itc: Supplier claims own ITC; no RCM applies
scenarios.notes: RCM does not apply once the supplier has opted to charge 12% with ITC.

services.intro: RCM applies only when the supplier is not a body corporate; the recipient's status also matters.

scenarios.supplier: Any person other than a body corporate (e.g. proprietorship, partnership security agency)
scenarios.notes: Excludes Government departments and composition dealers as recipients — for them, forward charge applies instead.

scenarios.option: Exception — supplier is a body corporate
scenarios.itc: Available to recipient in the normal course
scenarios.notes: RCM notification specifically excludes body corporate suppliers.

scenarios.supplier: Individual advocate, senior advocate, or firm of advocates
scenarios.recipient: Any business entity with turnover above the applicable threshold
scenarios.notes: Services to non-business individuals, or to entities below threshold, are exempt — no RCM arises.
Sponsorship to individuals/other entity types stays under forward charge or exempt as applicable.

scenarios.rate: As applicable to the underlying service
scenarios.notes: Excludes renting of immovable property and specifically excluded services (e.g. postal, transport of goods/passengers), which follow their own rules.

scenarios.supplier: Director (in non-employee capacity — sitting fees, commission)
scenarios.notes: Salary to a whole-time director under employment is outside GST altogether.

scenarios.supplier: Author who has filed the option to pay forward charge
scenarios.itc: Supplier claims own ITC; no RCM
scenarios.notes: Available specifically to authors, via a declaration filed with the jurisdictional officer.

scenarios.supplier: Lender (owner of securities, via approved intermediary)

scenarios.option: Residential dwelling — let to a business
scenarios.recipient: Registered person, where the dwelling is used for business purposes
scenarios.notes: Effective 18-Jul-2022. Renting for purely personal residential use by a registered person is not covered.

scenarios.rate: 18% (with exemption up to unsold units at completion)

scenarios.option: Any import of service for consideration
scenarios.supplier: Foreign supplier with no establishment in India
scenarios.recipient: Any person in India (business or non-business)
scenarios.itc: Available to recipient if used for business
scenarios.notes: Applies even to one-off, non-business imports (software licences, consultancy, subscriptions). Certain OIDAR-to-consumer imports instead require the foreign supplier itself to register in India.
